paper.title: Sequential C–O decarboxylative vinylation/C–H arylation of cyclic oxalates via a nickel-catalyzed multicomponent radical cascade

declarations.competing_interests: Not stated in the converted text.

definitions.definition: One-step reaction of a cyclic alkyl oxalate (caesium salt), a terminal alkyne and an aryl halide: decarboxylative alkyl radical addition to the alkyne, 1,5-hydrogen atom transfer from the ring to the vinyl radical, and nickel-catalysed arylation of the ring carbon radical.

Alkyne 0.1 mmol, cyclic oxalate 3.0 equiv, aryl halide 2.0 equiv, Ir[dF(CF3)ppy]2(dtbbpy)PF6 2 mol%, NiCl2(Py)4 20 mol%, dtbbpy 20 mol%, bis(4-methoxyphenyl)methanone 10 mol%, DMSO 0.05 M, 37 °C, 90 W blue LEDs.
Products carrying a trans-alkenyl group and an aryl group on carbons 1 and 3 of a saturated ring, formed as roughly 1:1 to 1:1.2 mixtures of diastereomers.
Isolated yield of product based on the alkyne, unless the source marks it as a crude 1H NMR yield.
The standard conditions with one component removed: photocatalyst, nickel catalyst, light, ligand or additive.
Standard conditions without the iridium photocatalyst.
Standard conditions without the nickel catalyst.
The radical formed when the alkyl radical adds to the alkyne, proposed to abstract a hydrogen atom from carbon 5 of its own chain (1,5-HAT).
Reaction under standard conditions with ethynylcyclopropane in place of the alkyne; ring opening to an allene indicates a vinyl radical.
The groups of the scope tables: cyclic oxalates, alkynes, aryl bromides, heteroaryl halides, aryl iodides and chlorides.
Products 4-14: varied five- and six-membered carbo- and heterocyclic oxalates.
Products 19-29: varied terminal aliphatic alkynes, including late-stage examples.

definitions.term: heteroaryl and other aryl halide scope
definitions.definition: Products 36-42: heteroaryl halides, aryl iodides and aryl chlorides.

claims.statement: Under the [[D2:standard conditions]], the [[D1:vinylation/arylation cascade]] gives [[D3:1,3-vinylarylated cycloalkanes]] from five- and six-membered cyclic oxalates, terminal aliphatic alkynes and aryl halides in 36% to 77% [[D4:yield]].
Compared with the [[D2:standard conditions]], each of the [[D5:control reactions]] that removes the photocatalyst, the nickel catalyst or light gives 0% [[D4:yield]].
The [[D1:vinylation/arylation cascade]] proceeds through a [[D9:vinyl radical intermediate]], as the [[D10:radical clock experiment]] gives the ring-opened allene.

evidence.description: Substrate scope: 39 products (4-42) under standard conditions, each from a single run with isolated yield; failures of 4- and 7-membered, bicyclic and linear oxalates reported in text.

tables.description: Range of yields per substrate class

availability.comment: Procedures and NMR spectra as images in the electronic supplementary information; no raw data deposited.

evidence.description: Optimisation and control reactions on the model reaction (oxalate 1, alkyne 2, 4-bromobenzonitrile 3); yields of product 4 by crude 1H NMR.

tables.description: Yield of product 4 under standard and control conditions

results.variable: yield of product 4 under standard conditions (crude 1H NMR)

evidence.description: Radical clock with ethynylcyclopropane gave allene 48; a stoichiometric aryl-Ni(II) complex did not give the 1,3-product; aryl alkynes gave 1,2-alkylarylation instead.

limitations.statement: Four- and seven-membered, bicyclic and linear oxalates and internal alkynes fail, so the scope is limited to five- and six-membered rings and terminal alkynes.
Products form as near 1:1 diastereomer mixtures; yields combine both diastereomers.
The authors note that a nickel(0) oxidative-addition pathway cannot be excluded.
